successors.name: House of Bourbon
successors.text: Bearn proper (bordered by Soule and Lower Navarre to the west, Gascony to the north, Bigorre to the east and Aragon to the south), drawn as the Pyrenees-Atlantiques cells within 50 km of Pau, plus…

ledger.x: 25 September 1347: Gaston Fébus declares Bearn sovereign.
1391: Fébus dies (1 August) and the Estates of Béarn name Matthew of Foix-Castelbon heir on 8 August; Charles VI recognised him as sole heir on 20 December 1391.
1407: Bigorre returns to the Foix lord.
ledger.cp: Bernard VII, Count of Armagnac (holder of Bigorre)

ledger.x: 1464: Gaston IV moves his court from Orthez to Pau, the capital from the mid-15th century (Bearn page).
1479: the lords of Béarn take the crown of Navarre.

12 February 1517: Catherine of Navarre dies at Mont-de-Marsan and her son Henry II, by John III of Albret, succeeds her (Catherine page); the lordship of Béarn passes from the Foix line to the Albret house.
25 May 1555: Bearn passes to the House of Bourbon.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War
wars.outcome: Fébus used the French defeat at Crécy (1346) to distance himself from France, was spared reprisals after Poitiers (1356), was compensated at the Treaty of Brétigny (8 May 1360) for the loss of Bigorre with 200,000 guilders and resisted the Black Prince, who…

certainty.note: Pyrenean valleys and the plain at their foot, with two exclaves in the east belonging to Bigorre (Bearn page); no treaty or survey line in the pages opened.
